Distribution and ecology. Known only from the type locality in which it is a common species with ca. 4 % relative abundance. The samples that included this species were scraped off surface of stones collected in the Xie River. Hence, this is a benthic, epilithic species. The associated taxa include Navicula reinhardtii Grunow, N. radiosa Kuetzing, Ulnaria hupingensis Bing Liu, U. xieriverensis Bing Liu and many unidentified Cymbella spp., Fragilaria spp., Gomphonema spp., amongst others. The following environmental parameters were measured in the field with three replications: Conductivity = 236.3 + / - 1.2 μS cm- 1; pH = 8.49 + / - 0.02; Water temperature = 13.6 + / - 0.1 ° C.

DISTRIBUTION. — Vanuatu (Malekula, Santo), Îles Salomon (Pauly & Munzinger 2003). DIAGNOSE. — Femelle (8 mm): tête jaune, deux bandes noires frontales convergeant sur le vertex; bandes noires du mesonotum séparées par des bandes jaunes plus étroites; bandes noires du scutellum deux fois plus larges que les bandes jaunes latérales; propodeum et côtés du thorax fauves; gastre fauve, les trois derniers segments apicaux noirs. Mâle: moitié inférieure de la face jaune.
Distribution: confined to the S. E. part of Yunnan; also found in N. E. Laos and N. Vietnam.
